descriptionHtml:
Approach · TC-11 Course Timeline · S08 Wrong device clock and another time zone show the same timeline as a correct device

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U9 'Today' on the timeline comes from the server clock, not the device's; a device with a wrong date, no clock set or a different time zone shows the same state as any other device. (UAT 3.8; TFA-92589 AC 7)
  • U3 Hospital: the timeline shows yesterday and today only, per the retention rules. (UAT TC-11; UAT 3.6; TFA-92589 AC 4)
  • U1 One entry per completed visit, correctly dated, in chronological order, never duplicated. (UAT TC-11; TFA-92589 AC 3)

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given Hospital ledger with lines for <day-2>, <day-1> and <day0> (server dates); a resident with no line today

When Open the Hospital chart from three browser profiles: correct clock; clock +1 day; correct clock but a time zone on the other side of the date line from the server's day (Asia/Tokyo vs America/New_York, run between 00:00 and 13:00 JST). From the +1-day profile, finish a Nursing Home note

Then All three profiles show the same Hospital cards (<day-1>, <day0>). The note finished from the +1-day profile is filed under the server's <day0>, not <day+1>. Sign-in works on every profile

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Cross-profile compare, scoped to the Course Timeline: the set of course cards in each snapshot equals the correct profile's. NH: 'Visit 1 – {day0}' present and '{day+1}' absent. The time-zone profile is Q4, recorded and judged once it is answered. Each profile's first checkpoint proves the chart opened. …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method MULTI · Multi-device / multi-account; lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (blocked)

S08 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-11.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 25acd727 (10-15/16 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: MULTI · Multi-device / multi-account; secondary: PW · Playwright script — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: TC-11 Course Timeline · Section: A2 · Pre-Round · Scenario: TC-11/S08

The Hospital ledger was seeded 'Oct 13: Admitted with volume overload' / 'Oct 14: Diuresis started' / 'Oct 15: Breathing easier' (day0 = the server instant cut in the host time zone, the build's reading; whose day it should be is Q4). correct (real clock, Asia/Tokyo) and ahead1d (clock +1 day) both show exactly the Oct 14 and Oct 15 cards, not Oct 13, and ahead1d already did on the first render. From ahead1d a Nursing Home note was finished (generateNote and refreshCourseAndBackground answered by the socket mock): the Visit Timeline reads 'Visit 1 – Oct 15: …' (the server's day, not Oct 16), stored as one line 'Visit 1 · Oct 15: …', and 'Encounter done' is gone. Sign-in: correct and otherTz opened with their stored sessions; ahead1d's stored session was dropped by its own clock (known B33) and signing in again through the form reached the app. Judged 8/8. Recorded for Q4, not judged: the America/New_York browser cuts the day in its own zone and shows different cards ('Oct 13: Admitted with volume overload', 'Oct 14: Diuresis started'), hiding the JST-today line.

Evidence: 5 attached.
